views.name: flights_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  flight_id,
  flight_no,
  scheduled_departure,
  scheduled_arrival,
  departure_airport,
  arrival_airport,
  status,
  aircraft_code,
  actual_departure,
  actual_arrival
FROM flights

params.description: Row-level normalized flight facts (one row per flight) with scheduled/actual times, origin/destination, status and aircraft — answers questions about individual flights and serves as a base for aggregations by time, airport, aircraft, status, etc.
params.when_to_use: Look up details for a specific flight_id or flight_no (scheduling and actual times, airports, status, aircraft). | Filter/select flights by departure/arrival airport, scheduled or actual times, status, or aircraft for downstream analysis. | Compose aggregations such as counts of flights, on-time/delayed tallies, average delays, or joins to bookings/tickets/aircraft/airport reference data while preserving one-row-per-flight granularity. | Serve as the normalized grain input when building flight-level metrics (delay per flight, flight counts) before aggregating to higher grains (date, airport, aircraft).
params.output_schema: flight_id: unique identifier for the flight at the flight (row) grain — derived directly from flights.flight_id | flight_no: carrier flight number or code identifying the flight — derived directly from flights.flight_no | scheduled_departure: scheduled departure timestamp for the flight — derived directly from flights.scheduled_departure | scheduled_arrival: scheduled arrival timestamp for the flight — derived directly from flights.scheduled_arrival | departure_airport: origin airport code or id for the flight — derived directly from flights.departure_airport | arrival_airport: destination airport code or id for the flight — derived directly from flights.arrival_airport | status: flight operational status (e.g., scheduled, cancelled, departed) — derived directly from flights.status | aircraft_code: aircraft identifier or type code assigned to this flight — derived directly from flights.aircraft_code | actual_departure: actual departure timestamp when the flight left — derived directly from flights.actual_departure | actual_arrival: actual arrival timestamp when the flight landed — derived directly from flights.actual_arrival
params.grounded_columns: flights.flight_id | flights.flight_no | flights.scheduled_departure | flights.scheduled_arrival | flights.departure_airport | flights.arrival_airport | flights.status | flights.aircraft_code | flights.actual_departure | flights.actual_arrival
params.metric: flight_count = COUNT(flight_id)  -- classic aggregate when counting flights; must be computed after grouping | departure_delay_seconds = EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (actual_departure - scheduled_departure))  -- per-flight delay measure (NULL if actual_departure is NULL); treat as a derived per-row metric, compute per-flight then aggregate (AVG, SUM, etc.) | arrival_delay_seconds = EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (actual_arrival - scheduled_arrival))  -- per-flight arrival delay measure (NULL if actual_arrival is NULL)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to aircrafts_reference on flights_basic.aircraft_code = aircrafts_reference.aircraft_code — safe because aircrafts_reference is a normalized reference table (one-row-per-aircraft_code) so joining enriches each flight without duplicating flights_basic rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to airports_reference on flights_basic.departure_airport = airports_reference.airport_code and/or flights_basic.arrival_airport = airports_reference.airport_code — safe because airports_reference is one-row-per-airport and will not duplicate flight rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to flight_rank_by_time on flights_basic.flight_id = flight_rank_by_time.flight_id — safe if flight_rank_by_time is one-row-per-flight_id (rank view name implies same grain); verify rank view's grain is flight_id before joining. | DO NOT join directly to ticket_segments_enriched without aggregation: ticket_segments_enriched is a one-to-many join (one flight -> many ticket segments). Joining it directly will multiply flights_basic rows and duplicate per-flight measures (e.g., flight_count). To combine, either aggregate ticket_segments_enriched to one row per flight_id first (for example SUM(passenger_count) or COUNT(ticket_segment_id) grouped by flight_id) and then join, or compute metrics by joining and then re-aggregating at the desired grain. | DO NOT join directly to boarding_with_seat_and_ticket without re-aggregation: boarding_with_seat_and_ticket is likely one-to-many per flight (multiple boardings/tickets per flight). Aggregate that data to one row per flight_id (e.g., boarded_count, seats_occupied) before joining, otherwise this view's rows/measures will be multiplied. | DO NOT join directly to bookings_revenue_by_date without aligning grain: bookings_revenue_by_date is an aggregate by booking date (not necessarily flight_id). If you need revenue per flight, either use a bookings-by-flight aggregate or join on a flight-specific key after ensuring bookings_revenue_by_date has one row per flight_id. Joining on date-level aggregates will duplicate or misattribute flight rows unless you first aggregate flights to the same date grain. | When composing with flights_delay_metrics (AGG): prefer joining on flight_id only if flights_delay_metrics has one-row-per-flight_id; if flights_delay_metrics is already aggregated to another grain (e.g., per-day), either aggregate flights_basic to that grain first (group by date derived from scheduled_departure) or use a pre-aggregated flights_delay_metrics keyed to that same grain to avoid duplication. | General rule: this view is one-row-per flight (flight_id). Any join target that is one-row-per-flight_id or genuinely reference-like (one row per key) is safe. Any join target that is one-to-many per flight_id must be reduced (aggregated) to one row per flight_id before joining, otherwise per-flight measures (counts, per-flight delay) will be multiplied.

views.description: Normalized projection of flights with deterministic columns and nullable-safe aliases. Use this as the canonical flights relation for joins and downstream analytics (scheduling, punctuality, joins to ticket segments). | Use for: flight on-time/delay analysis; join tickets/ticket_flights to flights; flight schedule listings and filtering by airport or status

views.name: flights_delay_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  flight_id,
  flight_no,
  departure_airport,
  arrival_airport,
  aircraft_code,
  scheduled_departure,
  actual_departure,
  scheduled_arrival,
  actual_arrival,
  CASE
    WHEN actual_departure IS NOT NULL AND scheduled_departure IS NOT NULL
    THEN CAST((julianday(actual_departure) - julianday(scheduled_departure)) * 24.0 * 60.0 AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS departure_delay_minutes,
  CASE
    WHEN actual_arrival IS NOT NULL AND scheduled_arrival IS NOT NULL
    THEN CAST((julianday(actual_arrival) - julianday(scheduled_arrival)) * 24.0 * 60.0 AS INTEGER)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS arrival_delay_minutes
FROM flights

params.description: Provides one-row-per-flight delay and schedule timing details (departure/arrival scheduled vs actual and computed minute delays).
params.when_to_use: Report or dashboard showing per-flight on-time performance (departure and arrival delay minutes). | Filter or drill into flights by airport, aircraft, flight number, or scheduled/actual times before joining to other dimensions. | Compose higher-level aggregations (e.g., average delay by airport/day/aircraft) by aggregating over this view's delay columns. | Enrich flight-level results with passenger, booking, or revenue data by joining on flight_id (with care — see composition).
params.output_schema: flight_id: Unique identifier for the flight. Derived directly from flights.flight_id. | flight_no: Flight number (carrier flight code). Derived directly from flights.flight_no. | departure_airport: IATA/airport code (origin). Derived directly from flights.departure_airport. | arrival_airport: IATA/airport code (destination). Derived directly from flights.arrival_airport. | aircraft_code: Aircraft type or tail identifier used for the flight. Derived directly from flights.aircraft_code. | scheduled_departure: Scheduled departure datetime/timestamp for the flight. Derived directly from flights.scheduled_departure. | actual_departure: Actual departure datetime/timestamp for the flight (nullable). Derived directly from flights.actual_departure. | scheduled_arrival: Scheduled arrival datetime/timestamp for the flight. Derived directly from flights.scheduled_arrival. | actual_arrival: Actual arrival datetime/timestamp for the flight (nullable). Derived directly from flights.actual_arrival. | departure_delay_minutes: Integer minutes difference (actual_departure - scheduled_departure) when both timestamps exist, else NULL. Computed as CAST((julianday(actual_departure) - julianday(scheduled_departure)) * 24.0 * 60.0 AS INTEGER) from flights.actual_departure and flights.scheduled_departure. | arrival_delay_minutes: Integer minutes difference (actual_arrival - scheduled_arrival) when both timestamps exist, else NULL. Computed as CAST((julianday(actual_arrival) - julianday(scheduled_arrival)) * 24.0 * 60.0 AS INTEGER) from flights.actual_arrival and flights.scheduled_arrival.
params.grounded_columns: flights.flight_id | flights.flight_no | flights.departure_airport | flights.arrival_airport | flights.aircraft_code | flights.scheduled_departure | flights.actual_departure | flights.scheduled_arrival | flights.actual_arrival
params.metric: departure_delay_minutes = CASE WHEN flights.actual_departure IS NOT NULL AND flights.scheduled_departure IS NOT NULL THEN CAST((julianday(flights.actual_departure) - julianday(flights.scheduled_departure)) * 24.0 * 60.0 AS INTEGER) ELSE NULL END | arrival_delay_minutes = CASE WHEN flights.actual_arrival IS NOT NULL AND flights.scheduled_arrival IS NOT NULL THEN CAST((julianday(flights.actual_arrival) - julianday(flights.scheduled_arrival)) * 24.0 * 60.0 AS INTEGER) ELSE NULL END
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to flights_basic on flight_id — safe because flights_basic is a 1:1/normalized row-per-flight (same grain) so this view's one-row-per-flight measures will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to aircrafts_reference on aircraft_code — safe because aircrafts_reference is a normalized reference dimension keyed by aircraft_code (one row per aircraft), so joining will not multiply flight rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to airports_reference on departure_airport = airports_reference.airport_code or arrival_airport = airports_reference.airport_code — safe because airports_reference is a normalized reference dimension (one row per airport). | cardinality-UNSAFE warning: do NOT directly join to one-to-many views/tables such as ticket_segments_enriched, boarding_with_seat_and_ticket, bookings_revenue_by_date, or passenger_segment_counts without aggregation, because those contain multiple rows per flight_id (tickets, segments, passengers, bookings) and would multiply this view's rows and thus distort per-flight measures. If you need aggregated passenger/ticket/revenue measures by flight, first aggregate those tables to one row per flight_id (e.g., SUM, COUNT grouped by flight_id) and then join to this view on flight_id. | cardinality-UNSAFE warning: do NOT join to flight_rank_by_time if it produces multiple ranks per flight_id (verify its grain). If flight_rank_by_time is one-row-per-flight, joining is safe; otherwise aggregate or filter to one row per flight before joining. | aggregation patterns: to compute airport/day averages or totals, GROUP BY departure_airport or arrival_airport and date(scheduled_departure) after selecting this view — do not join raw one-to-many passenger tables first. | preserve measures: because this view is one-row-per-flight (grain flight_id), any composition that preserves that cardinality (1:1 or many-to-1 to dimension/reference tables) will keep departure_delay_minutes and arrival_delay_minutes correct without re-aggregation.

views.description: Per-flight derived delay measures: departure_delay_minutes and arrival_delay_minutes computed when actual timestamps are present. Useful to summarize punctuality or compute aggregates by aircraft, route, or date. | Use for: compute average delay by route/aircraft/day; identify delayed flights; percent on-time vs delayed

views.name: ticket_segments_enriched
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  tf.ticket_no,
  tf.flight_id,
  tf.fare_conditions,
  tf.amount,
  t.book_ref,
  t.passenger_id,
  b.book_date,
  b.total_amount
FROM ticket_flights tf
LEFT JOIN tickets t ON tf.ticket_no = t.ticket_no
LEFT JOIN bookings b ON t.book_ref = b.book_ref

params.description: Provides one-row-per-ticket-flight enriched with ticket and booking attributes to answer questions about fares, booking context, and passenger associations for each ticket-flight (grain: ticket_no + flight_id).
params.when_to_use: Look up fare_conditions and fare amount for a specific ticket on a specific flight. | Combine ticket-flight fare data with booking-level attributes (book_date, total_amount) for revenue/time analyses at ticket-flight grain. | Filter or group by passenger_id or book_ref while preserving the ticket-flight-level measures. | As a base for further aggregation (e.g., revenue per passenger, per booking date) — aggregate after joining to avoid double counting.
params.output_schema: ticket_no: ticket identifier at the ticket level — derived from ticket_flights.ticket_no | flight_id: flight identifier — derived from ticket_flights.flight_id | fare_conditions: fare class/conditions for this ticket-flight — derived from ticket_flights.fare_conditions | amount: fare amount charged for this ticket-flight (monetary) — derived from ticket_flights.amount | book_ref: booking reference linking ticket to a booking — derived from tickets.book_ref | passenger_id: passenger identifier associated with the ticket — derived from tickets.passenger_id | book_date: booking date for the booking that contains this ticket — derived from bookings.book_date | total_amount: total booking amount for the booking that contains this ticket (monetary) — derived from bookings.total_amount
params.grounded_columns: ticket_flights.ticket_no | ticket_flights.flight_id | ticket_flights.fare_conditions | ticket_flights.amount | tickets.ticket_no | tickets.book_ref | tickets.passenger_id | bookings.book_ref | bookings.book_date | bookings.total_amount
params.metric: amount = direct column ticket_flights.amount (row-level monetary measure at ticket_no+flight_id grain) | total_amount = direct column bookings.total_amount (booking-level monetary attribute repeated for each ticket that references the booking) | no derived aggregates are computed in this view; any aggregates (SUM, AVG, COUNT) must be computed by the downstream query at the chosen grain
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to bookings_revenue_by_date (AGG) on bookings.book_date = bookings_revenue_by_date.book_date — safe because bookings_revenue_by_date is aggregated by book_date (one row per date) so joining will not duplicate ticket-flight rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to airports_reference or aircrafts_reference (NORM) via a flight-level view (e.g., flights_basic) only after joining flights_basic on flight_id — safe if you join ticket_segments_enriched -> flights_basic (1:1 per flight_id) then flights_basic -> airports/aircrafts (1:1 lookup). Do not join airports_reference directly to ticket_segments_enriched without ensuring a single flight row per flight_id. | do NOT join directly to a sibling AGG view that is many-to-one to this view's grain without aggregating this view first: e.g., do NOT join ticket_segments_enriched directly to passenger_segment_counts (AGG) on passenger_id if passenger_segment_counts is at a different grain (e.g., passenger + segment) that can be many rows per passenger, unless you intend to multiply ticket rows; instead aggregate ticket_segments_enriched to passenger_id first (e.g., SUM(amount) GROUP BY passenger_id) and then join to passenger_segment_counts. | do NOT join to boarding_with_seat_and_ticket (JOIN) or any other ticket-level JOIN that can have multiple boarding rows per ticket without re-aggregation, because boarding_with_seat_and_ticket may be one-to-many from ticket_no to boarding events — such a join would duplicate amount and booking-level attributes. If you need boarding details, either aggregate boarding to ticket_no first (e.g., COUNT(boardings) or MAX(seat)) or aggregate ticket_segments_enriched after joining. | safe composition pattern for downstream aggregations: when computing metrics like total fare per booking_date or per passenger, aggregate ticket_segments_enriched (e.g., SUM(amount) GROUP BY book_date) rather than joining ticket_segments_enriched to a one-to-many detail and then summing without DISTINCT/aggregation. | joins that preserve measures: joining to flights_basic(NORM) on flight_id is safe provided flights_basic is one-row-per-flight_id (it is NORM). Joining to flight-level AGG or RANK views is safe only when those views are one-row-per-flight_id; verify sibling view grain before joining. | summary rule: only join this view to dimension/lookup views that are one-row-per-key (flight_id, passenger_id, book_ref, book_date) to avoid duplicating ticket-level amount. If joining to any view that can have multiple rows per ticket_no or per booking (one-to-many), re-aggregate measures from ticket_segments_enriched first or perform the corresponding aggregation on the joined data to maintain cardinality-safe measures.

views.description: Denormalized one-row-per ticket segment combining ticket_flights with ticket and booking metadata. Preserves ticket and booking keys for downstream aggregation by passenger or booking. | Use for: revenue per ticket segment; passenger-level spending and segments; join segments to flights/schedules

views.name: boarding_with_seat_and_ticket
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  bp.ticket_no,
  bp.flight_id,
  bp.boarding_no,
  bp.seat_no,
  t.passenger_id,
  t.book_ref,
  s.aircraft_code AS seats_aircraft_code,
  s.seat_no AS seats_seat_no,
  s.fare_conditions AS seats_fare_conditions
FROM boarding_passes bp
LEFT JOIN tickets t ON bp.ticket_no = t.ticket_no
LEFT JOIN seats s ON s.aircraft_code = (
    SELECT aircraft_code FROM flights f WHERE f.flight_id = bp.flight_id
  ) AND s.seat_no = bp.seat_no

params.description: Provides one row per boarding event (ticket + flight + boarding number) enriched with the passenger, booking reference, and the matching seat attributes from the aircraft's seat map.
params.when_to_use: Look up seat and passenger/booking info for a specific boarding event (ticket_no + flight_id + boarding_no). | Build downstream views/queries that need per-boarding detail (seat_no, passenger_id, book_ref) as the grain. | Compose aggregations by boarding event (e.g., counts of boardings, distinct passengers per flight, seat-based metrics) by aggregating this view. | Join flight-level or ticket-level reference data to boarding-level analytics without changing boarding-level cardinality (when joined on one-to-one/one-to-many keys described below).
params.output_schema: ticket_no: boarding_passes.ticket_no — identifier of the ticket associated with this boarding record (base column from boarding_passes). | flight_id: boarding_passes.flight_id — identifier of the flight for this boarding event (base column from boarding_passes). | boarding_no: boarding_passes.boarding_no — boarding sequence/number within the ticket+flight grain (base column from boarding_passes). | seat_no: boarding_passes.seat_no — seat code assigned in the boarding_passes row (base column from boarding_passes). | passenger_id: tickets.passenger_id — passenger identifier pulled by left-joining tickets on ticket_no (base column from tickets). | book_ref: tickets.book_ref — booking reference pulled from tickets (base column from tickets). | seats_aircraft_code: seats.aircraft_code — aircraft code from seats matched to the flight's aircraft (base column from seats via the correlated subquery to flights). | seats_seat_no: seats.seat_no — seat identifier from the seats table (base column from seats). | seats_fare_conditions: seats.fare_conditions — fare/seat class information from seats (base column from seats).
params.grounded_columns: boarding_passes.ticket_no | boarding_passes.flight_id | boarding_passes.boarding_no | boarding_passes.seat_no | tickets.ticket_no | tickets.passenger_id | tickets.book_ref | seats.aircraft_code | seats.seat_no | seats.fare_conditions | flights.flight_id | flights.aircraft_code
params.metric: This view contains no aggregated measures. All columns are raw/normalized attributes at the grain (ticket_no, flight_id, boarding_no). | If you derive metrics on top of this view, define them by aggregating over the view's grain. Examples: | boardings_count = COUNT(*)  -- number of boarding events (count of rows) at the aggregation keys you choose | distinct_passengers = COUNT(DISTINCT passenger_id)  -- count of unique passengers in the aggregation set | seat_assignments_per_flight = COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE seat_no IS NOT NULL)  -- number of assigned seats in aggregation set
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: | Join to flights_basic (or flights_* views keyed by flight_id) on flight_id — safe because flights_basic is one-row-per-flight (one-to-one with this view's flight_id). Joining on flights_basic.flight_id will not duplicate boarding rows. | Join to aircrafts_reference on aircraft_code = seats_aircraft_code (or aircraft_code = flights.aircraft_code if you join flights first) — safe because aircrafts_reference is one-row-per-aircraft_code (one-to-one). | Join to airports_reference on a flight-level airport key (after joining flights_basic) — safe if you join using the flight's origin/destination airport_code from flights_basic (one-to-one per flight). Do not join airports_reference directly to this view without first joining flights_basic, because this view does not contain airport_code. | Join to ticket_segments_enriched on ticket_no — safe only if ticket_segments_enriched is one-row-per-ticket (verify its grain). If ticket_segments_enriched is one-to-many (multiple segments per ticket), joining directly will multiply boarding rows and thus duplicate counts; in that case aggregate ticket_segments_enriched to ticket_no (e.g., choose MIN/MAX or COUNT of segments) before joining. | Do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many detail table/view (e.g., passenger_segment_counts, bookings_revenue_by_date, flights_delay_metrics, or any segments/leg-level view) without re-aggregating the one-to-many side to the join key. These sibling views are labelled AGG and may be at a different grain (e.g., per-flight, per-booking-date, per-passenger) and can duplicate rows if their grain is finer or multi-row per boarding key. | If you need to enrich this view with aggregated metrics from sibling AGG views: | - For flight-level aggregates (flights_delay_metrics, flight_rank_by_time): aggregate this view up to flight_id (or join the AGG view to a one-row-per-flight subquery of this view) so the flight-level metric aligns with the flight grain. | - For booking-level aggregates (bookings_revenue_by_date): aggregate this view to book_ref before joining, or aggregate the AGG to book_ref if it has a finer grain. | - For passenger-level aggregates (passenger_segment_counts): aggregate that table to passenger_id before joining to avoid multiplying boarding rows when passenger has multiple segments. | Rationale: This view's declared grain is (ticket_no, flight_id, boarding_no) — one row per boarding event. Any join to another dataset that is one-to-one with these keys preserves cardinality. Joins to datasets that are one-to-many w.r.t these keys will multiply rows and thus duplicate any derived counts or sums unless the many-side is pre-aggregated to a one-row-per-key form.

views.description: One row per boarding_pass enriched with ticket passenger and seat configuration (when available). Helpful to reconcile assigned seat_no with aircraft seat map and fare class. | Use for: seat assignment consistency checks; boarding lists and passenger-seat lookups; analyse fare class distribution by actual assigned seats

views.name: aircrafts_reference
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  aircraft_code,
  model,
  range
FROM aircrafts_data

params.description: Reference lookup of aircrafts: returns one row per aircraft_code with its model and range.
params.when_to_use: Enrich flight or booking records with aircraft model or range by joining on aircraft_code. | Filter or group analyses by aircraft model or range. | Compose aggregations that need aircraft-level attributes (e.g., average range by model).
params.output_schema: aircraft_code: unique identifier for the aircraft type/code — derived directly from aircrafts_data.aircraft_code | model: aircraft model name/description — derived directly from aircrafts_data.model | range: numeric or reported range (distance capability) of the aircraft — derived directly from aircrafts_data.range
params.metric: No aggregate metrics are defined in this view; all output columns are direct pass-throughs: aircraft_code = aircrafts_data.aircraft_code, model = aircrafts_data.model, range = aircrafts_data.range
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to flights_basic on flights_basic.aircraft_code = aircrafts_reference.aircraft_code — safe because aircrafts_reference is one-row-per-aircraft_code, so joining will not duplicate aircraft-level attributes when enriching many flight rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to ticket_segments_enriched on ticket_segments_enriched.aircraft_code = aircrafts_reference.aircraft_code — safe for enrichment; ticket_segments_enriched may be many rows per flight/booking but this view remains one row per aircraft_code. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to boarding_with_seat_and_ticket on boarding_with_seat_and_ticket.aircraft_code = aircrafts_reference.aircraft_code — safe for enrichment; does not duplicate this view's rows because aircrafts_reference is at aircraft_code grain. | do NOT join without care to AGG views that are at lower grain (many-per-aircraft) unless you re-aggregate after the join: for example, do NOT join aircrafts_reference to a hypothetical per-flight aggregated metrics view (e.g., flights_delay_metrics) and then SUM range or other aircraft-level attributes across flights without first deciding whether range should be weighted or deduplicated — such joins could multiply aircraft rows across multiple flights and produce incorrect totals. | If combining with flights_delay_metrics (an AGG view): join on aircraft_code only when the AGG is at aircraft_code grain (one row per aircraft_code). If flights_delay_metrics is at flight-level aggregates (one row per flight), treat it as many-to-one (many flights -> one aircraft) and aggregate/combine results after the join to avoid duplicating any intended aircraft-level measures. | Safe to join to airports_reference on airport codes only if join keys are independent (e.g., origin_airport or dest_airport on flight views). aircrafts_reference does not reference airports, so joins between aircrafts_reference and airports_reference are unrelated and will produce a Cartesian effect unless mediated by a flight/ticket/boarding table.

views.description: Pass-through of aircrafts_data providing aircraft_code and model and range. Keep model as-is (jsonb) so callers decide localization. Use for joins and aircraft-level summaries. | Use for: lookup aircraft model or range; join aircraft attributes to flights for capacity/range analysis

views.name: airports_reference
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  airport_code,
  airport_name,
  city,
  coordinates,
  timezone
FROM airports_data

params.description: Reference lookup of airports by airport_code with static attributes (name, city, coordinates, timezone).
params.when_to_use: When you need airport metadata for display, filtering, or joining to flight/booking records by airport_code. | To enrich flight, booking, ticket, or aircraft data with airport name, city, coordinates, or timezone. | To build aggregated reports grouped by airport_code where airport attributes are required (join this view as a dimension).
params.output_schema: airport_code: IATA/ICAO airport identifier (derived directly from airports_data.airport_code). | airport_name: Official airport name (derived directly from airports_data.airport_name). | city: City where the airport is located (derived directly from airports_data.city). | coordinates: Geospatial point or lat/lon string for the airport location (derived directly from airports_data.coordinates). | timezone: Time zone identifier for the airport (derived directly from airports_data.timezone).
params.metric: No derived metrics in this view. All output columns are direct passthroughs from base columns: airport_code = airports_data.airport_code, airport_name = airports_data.airport_name, city = airports_data.city, coordinates = airports_data.coordinates, timezone = airports_data.timezone
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to flights_basic on flights_basic.origin_airport_code = airports_reference.airport_code or flights_basic.destination_airport_code = airports_reference.airport_code — safe because airports_reference is one-row-per-airport_code and therefore will not duplicate flight measures (each flight row joins to at most one airport row). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to flights_delay_metrics (an AGG) on flights_delay_metrics.airport_code = airports_reference.airport_code — safe because flights_delay_metrics is already aggregated per airport_code; joining to this one-row-per-airport reference will not multiply metrics. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to bookings_revenue_by_date on bookings_revenue_by_date.airport_code = airports_reference.airport_code — safe when bookings_revenue_by_date is aggregated per airport_code (it is an AGG), so no duplication occurs. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to ticket_segments_enriched, boarding_with_seat_and_ticket, passenger_segment_counts, or any other one-to-many detail table on airport_code if those tables contain multiple rows per airport (e.g., many tickets or boardings at the same airport) because that would multiply aggregated measures from airports_reference if mistakenly treated as measures. Instead, either: (a) aggregate the one-to-many table to one row per airport_code first, or (b) use airports_reference only as a dimension and keep measures on the detail side. | When composing with flight_rank_by_time (RANK) or other ranking views, verify their grain: if they are one-row-per-flight or one-row-per-flight-time they can be joined to airports_reference on airport_code safely (airports_reference remains one-row-per-airport). If a ranking view is one-to-many per airport, first aggregate/rank to a single row per airport_code before joining if you need airport-level uniqueness.

views.description: Pass-through of airports_data exposing airport_code and localized blobs. Consumers should extract language from airport_name and city jsonb. Useful for joins and geospatial lookups. | Use for: airport lookups by code; map flights by departure/arrival airport coordinates; filter flights by timezone or city

views.name: flight_rank_by_time
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  flight_id,
  departure_airport,
  scheduled_departure,
  scheduled_arrival,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY departure_airport ORDER BY scheduled_departure) AS departure_rank
FROM flights

params.description: Provides a per-flight rank (departure order) within each departure airport based on scheduled departure time.
params.when_to_use: Determine the sequence or position of a flight among other flights departing the same airport (e.g., 'Which flight is the 3rd scheduled departure from JFK today?'). | Compose time-based sequencing features for downstream analyses (e.g., relative ordering of flights for delay propagation models). | Join with other per-flight detail or metric views when you need the flight's rank as an attribute (e.g., enrich flight-level delay metrics with departure_rank).
params.output_schema: flight_id: unique identifier of the flight (derived from flights.flight_id) | departure_airport: airport code/identifier where the flight departs (derived from flights.departure_airport) | scheduled_departure: scheduled departure timestamp/time (derived from flights.scheduled_departure) | scheduled_arrival: scheduled arrival timestamp/time (derived from flights.scheduled_arrival) | departure_rank: integer rank of this flight among flights with the same departure_airport ordered by scheduled_departure (derived from RANK() window over flights.partition by departure_airport order by scheduled_departure)
params.metric: departure_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY flights.departure_airport ORDER BY flights.scheduled_departure)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to flights_basic (NORM) on flight_id — safe because flight_rank_by_time is one-row-per-flight (grain = flight_id) and flights_basic is likewise one-row-per-flight, so joining preserves row-uniqueness and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to flights_delay_metrics (AGG) on flight_id — safe only if flights_delay_metrics is aggregated to flight_id (one-row-per-flight). Confirm flights_delay_metrics' grain is flight_id before joining; if it is, measures won't be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to aircrafts_reference or airports_reference (NORM) on aircraft or airport key (e.g., departure_airport = airports_reference.airport_id) — safe because reference tables are one-row-per-entity (dimension), so they do not duplicate flight rows. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as ticket_segments_enriched (JOIN), boarding_with_seat_and_ticket (JOIN), bookings_revenue_by_date (AGG by date), or passenger_segment_counts (AGG by passenger/segment) without re-aggregation: those are one-to-many relative to flight_id and will multiply this view's rows/measures. If you need aggregated results after joining, first aggregate the one-to-many side back to flight_id (or the desired grain), then join. | When composing additional metrics that sum or count (e.g., total_tickets, total_revenue), ensure aggregation is applied after any join to many-sided views so you do not double-count. Preferred pattern: SELECT f.*, agg.* FROM flight_rank_by_time f JOIN (SELECT flight_id, SUM(...) AS ... FROM ticket_segments_enriched GROUP BY flight_id) agg USING (flight_id). | Because departure_rank is a window function value defined per flight within departure_airport, joining to another one-row-per-flight source keyed by flight_id will not change departure_rank values. Avoid joining multiple ranked views partitioned differently without explicit disambiguation, as combining ranks with different partitions may require recomputation.

views.description: Ranks flights per departure_airport by scheduled_departure time. Exposes departure_rank so callers can filter for earliest or latest N flights per airport without hardcoding a limit. | Use for: top-N earliest flights per airport; sampling flights around schedule boundaries

views.name: bookings_revenue_by_date
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(book_date) AS book_date,
  COUNT(*) AS bookings_count,
  SUM(total_amount) AS bookings_total_amount
FROM bookings
GROUP BY DATE(book_date)

params.description: Daily aggregated booking counts and total booked amount by booking date.
params.when_to_use: When you need daily totals of bookings and money booked (e.g., revenue by booking date). | As a building block for time series of booking volume or booked revenue at the booking-date grain. | To join to date or calendar reference tables for enrichment (weekday, month, fiscal period) without re-aggregating. | To compute rates or averages per booking day when combined with compatible denominators at the same day grain.
params.output_schema: book_date: DATE(bookings.book_date) — the booking date truncated to date (the GROUP BY grain). | bookings_count: COUNT(*) — number of booking rows on that book_date (derived from COUNT(*) over bookings rows in that date). | bookings_total_amount: SUM(total_amount) — sum of bookings.total_amount for that book_date (derived from SUM(bookings.total_amount)).
params.metric: bookings_count = COUNT(*) (count of bookings rows per DATE(book_date)) | bookings_total_amount = SUM(bookings.total_amount) (sum of the bookings.total_amount per DATE(book_date))
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE joins (do not duplicate measures): | Join to a date/calendar dimension (e.g., on date_dim.date = bookings_revenue_by_date.book_date) — safe because bookings_revenue_by_date has one row per book_date and date_dim is at most one row per date. | Join to single-row-per-date aggregates or views (e.g., other AGG views that are also one-row-per-book_date) on book_date — safe when the other view is guaranteed to be at the same DATE(book_date) grain so rows align 1:1. | Unsafe to join directly without re-aggregation: | Do NOT join bookings_revenue_by_date directly to any one-to-many child table or view keyed by book_date that contains multiple rows per date (for example raw bookings rows, ticket_segments_enriched, boarding_with_seat_and_ticket, or any N-of-M detail tables) because such joins will multiply bookings_count and bookings_total_amount. If you must combine with one-to-many detail, either: | - Re-aggregate the detail side to the same book_date grain before joining, or | - Join on a unique key (e.g., booking_id) after expanding bookings_revenue_by_date back to bookings (not possible from this aggregated view), or | - Use analytic-safe operations: compute ratios or rates by dividing two measures that were aggregated consistently at the same grain. | Notes on siblings: do NOT assume 1:1 joins to JOIN-type sibling views (ticket_segments_enriched, boarding_with_seat_and_ticket) unless those siblings have been pre-aggregated to DATE(book_date); joining them as-is will duplicate the aggregated measures. Joining to reference/norm tables (aircrafts_reference, airports_reference) is safe only when the join keys are unique on the reference side and the join is performed via a dimension that is already 1:1 with book_date (e.g., via a date dimension).

views.description: Daily aggregates of booking revenue and counts by book_date (date-truncated). Useful for trends, time-series, and rolling analyses. Does not assume timezone conversion; keeps book_date as source provides. | Use for: daily revenue/time trends; compare booking volume vs revenue

views.name: passenger_segment_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.passenger_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tf.flight_id) AS segments_count,
  SUM(tf.amount) AS segments_total_amount
FROM tickets t
LEFT JOIN ticket_flights tf ON t.ticket_no = tf.ticket_no
GROUP BY t.passenger_id

params.description: Per-passenger counts and total amount of flight segments referenced by that passenger's tickets.
params.when_to_use: Get the number of distinct flight segments and total segment amount for each passenger (passenger-level segment activity). | Compose passenger-level revenue/usage measures into larger analyses (e.g., join to passenger demographic/profile data or bookings) without re-aggregating passenger-level segment metrics. | Filter or roll up passengers by segment activity (e.g., find passengers with >N segments or high total segment amount) as a pre-aggregation for downstream joins/aggregations.
params.output_schema: passenger_id: passenger identifier from tickets.passenger_id — the grain of this view (one row per passenger). | segments_count: COUNT(DISTINCT tf.flight_id) — number of distinct flight segments associated to any ticket of the passenger as counted from ticket_flights.flight_id. | segments_total_amount: SUM(tf.amount) — sum of ticket_flights.amount for all ticket_flights rows tied to the passenger's tickets (NULLs from the LEFT JOIN are treated as absent; SUM over no rows yields NULL or 0 depending on SQL dialect).
params.metric: segments_count = COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_flights.flight_id) aggregated at passenger_id (derived from JOIN of tickets -> ticket_flights). | segments_total_amount = SUM(ticket_flights.amount) aggregated at passenger_id (derived from JOIN of tickets -> ticket_flights).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to passenger/profile dimensions (a hypothetical passengers table or view keyed by passenger_id) on passenger_id — safe because passenger_segment_counts is one-row-per-passenger and joining to a one-row-per-passenger dimension preserves measures without duplication. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to bookings_revenue_by_date ON passenger_id (if that view is one-row-per-passenger or one-row-per-passenger-date and you join at the same grain) — safe only when the join key preserves the same grain; if bookings_revenue_by_date is one-row-per-(passenger_id,date) then join on both passenger_id and date to avoid duplicating passenger-level aggregates. | DO NOT join directly to ticket_flights or ticket_segments_enriched (one-to-many from passenger -> ticket_flights) without re-aggregation: joining this aggregated view back to ticket_flights or any detailed segment-level table will multiply segments_count and segments_total_amount because those detail tables have multiple rows per passenger. If you need segment-level detail with these metrics, either (a) join and then re-aggregate, or (b) join to ticket_flights first and compute passenger metrics in the same query. | DO NOT join to booking/ticket-level JOINs that are one-to-many to tickets (e.g., ticket_segments_enriched or boarding_with_seat_and_ticket) without re-aggregation: those joins can produce multiple rows per passenger and will duplicate the aggregated measures. Instead, aggregate the joined data to passenger_id before combining with this view. | Safe to join to flight-level reference dimensions flights_basic or airports_reference or aircrafts_reference when joining on flight_id (or airport/aircraft keys) only if you first expand this view by re-joining at passenger->flight grain with careful re-aggregation: direct join of this view to flight-level tables on flight_id is not possible because this view does not contain flight_id — doing a multi-step plan must ensure you don't multiply rows. Prefer joining flight-level references to detailed flight rows (ticket_flights) and then compute passenger aggregates. | When composing with other AGG sibling views (e.g., flights_delay_metrics) ensure the join keys and grains align. Joining two aggregated views is safe only when one can guarantee one-to-one or many-to-one relationship between rows (e.g., both are one-row-per-passenger) — otherwise re-aggregate after the join. | Planner guidance: treat passenger_segment_counts as a passenger-level pre-aggregation. To combine with any lower-grain (ticket, flight, boarding) data, either (1) push aggregations down into the planner so the planner computes compatible group-bys, or (2) join at passenger_id and then re-aggregate to a desired grain to avoid measure duplication.

views.description: Counts and total amount per passenger (passenger_id) across their ticket segments. Useful to rank passengers by spend or segments and to detect high-value customers. | Use for: identify top passengers by spend or segments; customer lifetime/usage summaries

views.name: flights_with_airports
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.flight_id,
  f.flight_no,
  f.departure_airport,
  f.arrival_airport,
  f.scheduled_departure,
  f.scheduled_arrival,
  f.status,
  f.aircraft_code,
  -- departure coordinates (point stored as (lng,lat))
  CAST(NULLIF(substr(a_dep.coordinates, 2, instr(a_dep.coordinates, ',')-2), '') AS FLOAT) AS dep_longitude,
  CAST(NULLIF(substr(a_dep.coordinates, instr(a_dep.coordinates, ',')+1, length(a_dep.coordinates)-instr(a_dep.coordinates, ',')-1), '') AS FLOAT) AS dep_latitude,
  -- arrival coordinates
  CAST(NULLIF(substr(a_arr.coordinates, 2, instr(a_arr.coordinates, ',')-2), '') AS FLOAT) AS arr_longitude,
  CAST(NULLIF(substr(a_arr.coordinates, instr(a_arr.coordinates, ',')+1, length(a_arr.coordinates)-instr(a_arr.coordinates, ',')-1), '') AS FLOAT) AS arr_latitude,
  -- English city names from jsonb (stored as text); extract simple JSON property "en"
  json_extract(a_dep.city, '$.en') AS dep_city_en,
  json_extract(a_arr.city, '$.en') AS arr_city_en
FROM flights_basic f
JOIN airports_reference a_dep
  ON f.departure_airport = a_dep.airport_code
JOIN airports_reference a_arr
  ON f.arrival_airport = a_arr.airport_code
WHERE
  a_dep.coordinates IS NOT NULL
  AND a_arr.coordinates IS NOT NULL
views.description: Denormalized flight rows joined to departure and arrival airport canonical data (coordinates and English city/name). Exposes flight identifiers, scheduled/actual times, status, aircraft_code, and both airports' codes, cities and coordinates. Filters out flights where either airport coordinates are missing by relying on airports_canonical.

views.name: flight_distances_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.flight_id AS flight_id,
  f.departure_airport AS departure_airport,
  f.arrival_airport AS arrival_airport,
  -- departure coordinates: extract latitude and longitude from airports_reference.coordinates (point stored as "x,y")
  CASE
    WHEN ar_dep.coordinates IS NOT NULL THEN
      CAST(
        trim(substr(ar_dep.coordinates, instr(ar_dep.coordinates, '(') + 1,
                  instr(ar_dep.coordinates, ',') - instr(ar_dep.coordinates, '(') - 1)
        ) AS REAL
      )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS dep_longitude,
  CASE
    WHEN ar_dep.coordinates IS NOT NULL THEN
      CAST(
        trim(substr(ar_dep.coordinates, instr(ar_dep.coordinates, ',') + 1,
                  instr(ar_dep.coordinates, ')') - instr(ar_dep.coordinates, ',') - 1)
        ) AS REAL
      )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS dep_latitude,
  -- arrival coordinates
  CASE
    WHEN ar_arr.coordinates IS NOT NULL THEN
      CAST(
        trim(substr(ar_arr.coordinates, instr(ar_arr.coordinates, '(') + 1,
                  instr(ar_arr.coordinates, ',') - instr(ar_arr.coordinates, '(') - 1)
        ) AS REAL
      )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS arr_longitude,
  CASE
    WHEN ar_arr.coordinates IS NOT NULL THEN
      CAST(
        trim(substr(ar_arr.coordinates, instr(ar_arr.coordinates, ',') + 1,
                  instr(ar_arr.coordinates, ')') - instr(ar_arr.coordinates, ',') - 1)
        ) AS REAL
      )
    ELSE NULL
  END AS arr_latitude,
  -- English city names from airport JSON
  CASE
    WHEN ar_dep.city IS NOT NULL THEN
      json_extract(ar_dep.city, '$.en')
    ELSE NULL
  END AS dep_city_en,
  CASE
    WHEN ar_arr.city IS NOT NULL THEN
      json_extract(ar_arr.city, '$.en')
    ELSE NULL
  END AS arr_city_en
FROM flights AS f
LEFT JOIN airports_data AS ar_dep ON f.departure_airport = ar_dep.airport_code
LEFT JOIN airports_data AS ar_arr ON f.arrival_airport = ar_arr.airport_code
WHERE
  -- intrinsic non-null coordinate filters: ensure numeric parts present after extraction
  ar_dep.coordinates IS NOT NULL
  AND ar_arr.coordinates IS NOT NULL
  AND trim(substr(ar_dep.coordinates, instr(ar_dep.coordinates, '(') + 1,
                  instr(ar_dep.coordinates, ',') - instr(ar_dep.coordinates, '(') - 1)
      ) != ''
  AND trim(substr(ar_dep.coordinates, instr(ar_dep.coordinates, ',') + 1,
                  instr(ar_dep.coordinates, ')') - instr(ar_dep.coordinates, ',') - 1)
      ) != ''
  AND trim(substr(ar_arr.coordinates, instr(ar_arr.coordinates, '(') + 1,
                  instr(ar_arr.coordinates, ',') - instr(ar_arr.coordinates, '(') - 1)
      ) != ''
  AND trim(substr(ar_arr.coordinates, instr(ar_arr.coordinates, ',') + 1,
                  instr(ar_arr.coordinates, ')') - instr(ar_arr.coordinates, ',') - 1)
      ) != ''
grain: flight_id -- one row per flight segment
views.description: Per-flight raw great-circle distance inputs: keeps flight ids with departure/arrival airport codes, coordinates and English city names. Does not apply the Haversine formula yet — prepares numeric lat/lon and exposes them for distance computation and various filters/aggregations.

views.name: airport_city_coords
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  airport_code,
  -- extract canonical English city name from JSON stored in city
  (CASE
     WHEN json_extract(city, '$.en') IS NOT NULL AND trim(json_extract(city, '$.en')) <> '' THEN json_extract(city, '$.en')
     ELSE NULL
   END) AS city_en,
  -- coordinates is a point stored as text like "(lon,lat)"; extract numeric values
  (CASE
     WHEN coordinates IS NOT NULL
       THEN CAST(trim(replace(substr(coordinates, 2, instr(coordinates, ',')-2), ' ', '')) AS REAL)
     ELSE NULL
   END) AS longitude,
  (CASE
     WHEN coordinates IS NOT NULL
       THEN CAST(trim(replace(substr(coordinates, instr(coordinates, ',')+1, length(coordinates)-instr(coordinates, ',')-1), ')', '')) AS REAL)
     ELSE NULL
   END) AS latitude,
  timezone
FROM airports_data
WHERE json_extract(city, '$.en') IS NOT NULL
  AND coordinates IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per airport with its canonical English city name and numeric longitude/latitude extracted from the coordinates point. Cleans NULL/missing JSON fields and exposes values useful for geographic joins and distance calculations.

views.name: flight_with_cities
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.flight_id,
  f.flight_no,
  f.departure_airport,
  f.arrival_airport,
  -- canonical English city names from departure and arrival airports
  ad_dep.city ->> 'en' AS dep_city_en,
  ad_arr.city ->> 'en' AS arr_city_en,
  -- coordinates: point stored as (longitude, latitude)
  CAST(strftime('%f', (substr(ad_dep.coordinates, instr(ad_dep.coordinates, '(')+1,
        instr(ad_dep.coordinates, ',') - instr(ad_dep.coordinates, '(')-1))) AS REAL) AS dep_longitude,
  CAST(strftime('%f', (substr(ad_dep.coordinates, instr(ad_dep.coordinates, ',')+1,
        instr(ad_dep.coordinates, ')') - instr(ad_dep.coordinates, ',')-1))) AS REAL) AS dep_latitude,
  CAST(strftime('%f', (substr(ad_arr.coordinates, instr(ad_arr.coordinates, '(')+1,
        instr(ad_arr.coordinates, ',') - instr(ad_arr.coordinates, '(')-1))) AS REAL) AS arr_longitude,
  CAST(strftime('%f', (substr(ad_arr.coordinates, instr(ad_arr.coordinates, ',')+1,
        instr(ad_arr.coordinates, ')') - instr(ad_arr.coordinates, ',')-1))) AS REAL) AS arr_latitude,
  f.scheduled_departure,
  f.scheduled_arrival,
  f.status,
  f.aircraft_code
FROM
  flights_basic f
  JOIN airports_reference ad_dep ON ad_dep.airport_code = f.departure_airport
  JOIN airports_reference ad_arr ON ad_arr.airport_code = f.arrival_airport
WHERE
  -- intrinsic filters: both airports must have English city and coordinates
  (ad_dep.city ->> 'en') IS NOT NULL
  AND (ad_arr.city ->> 'en') IS NOT NULL
  AND ad_dep.coordinates IS NOT NULL
  AND ad_arr.coordinates IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per flight with departure and arrival airport codes joined to canonical English city names and numeric coordinates (both airports). Filters out flights where either airport lacks a valid English city or coordinates. Keeps scheduled/actual times and aircraft info for flexibility.

views.name: city_pair_flight_distances
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fdr.flight_id,
  CASE
    WHEN fdr.dep_city_en <= fdr.arr_city_en THEN fdr.dep_city_en
    ELSE fdr.arr_city_en
  END AS city_a,
  CASE
    WHEN fdr.dep_city_en <= fdr.arr_city_en THEN fdr.arr_city_en
    ELSE fdr.dep_city_en
  END AS city_b,
  -- Haversine formula: distance_km
  (
    6371.0 * 2.0 * ASIN(
      MIN(1.0,
        SQRT(
          POWER(SIN((RADIANS(fdr.arr_latitude - fdr.dep_latitude)) / 2.0), 2.0)
          +
          COS(RADIANS(fdr.dep_latitude)) * COS(RADIANS(fdr.arr_latitude))
          * POWER(SIN((RADIANS(fdr.arr_longitude - fdr.dep_longitude)) / 2.0), 2.0)
        )
      )
    )
  ) AS distance_km
FROM flight_distances_raw fdr
WHERE
  -- intrinsic filter: exclude rows where computed distance would be NULL due to missing coordinates
  fdr.dep_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND fdr.dep_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND fdr.arr_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND fdr.arr_longitude IS NOT NULL
grain: flight_id -- one row per flight (with canonical city pair and that flight's distance)
views.description: Aggregates flights by canonical unordered city pair (alphabetically sorted city names) and computes per-flight great-circle distance (Haversine inputs: radians of lat/lon) and exposes raw distances so downstream queries can compute averages and binning. One row per flight with canonical city pair fields to allow grouping later.
